description: DocuMind evaluation set. Every answer and evidence quote was checked by hand against the source file. 'evidence' holds verbatim quotes (whitespace-insensitive) that a correct retrieval must surface; a retrieved chunk counts as relevant when it contains one of them. 'must_contain' lists the key facts an answer has to state to be counted correct. 'follow_up_of' chains a question onto an earlier one in the same conversation. 'documents' with more than one entry are cross-document questions run through a workspace.

questions.question: What methodology does the paper use?
questions.answer: A hybrid retrieval approach combining BM25 lexical search with dense semantic embeddings, feeding top-ranked chunks to an LLM for grounded answer generation.

questions.question: What weighting is used to combine semantic and lexical scores?
questions.answer: 0.6 for semantic similarity and 0.4 for lexical relevance.

questions.question: How large was the evaluation dataset?
questions.answer: 120 question-answer pairs across five source documents.

questions.question: How many source documents was it drawn from?
questions.answer: Five source documents: two academic papers, two university regulation documents, and one technical manual.
evidence:
manually
verified against five source documents

questions.question: What Precision@5 did hybrid retrieval achieve?
And how did the BM25-only baseline do on that metric?
questions.answer: The BM25-only baseline reached a Precision@5 of 0.68.

questions.question: What is the main limitation of the approach?
questions.answer: It relies on well-structured source documents; scanned or image-only PDFs need a separate OCR pipeline, and it struggles with questions that need synthesis across many distant sections.

questions.question: How many words are in each chunk?
questions.answer: Approximately 220 words.

questions.question: What is the dimensionality of the embedding vectors?
questions.answer: 384-dimensional vectors.

questions.question: What kind of index is used for nearest-neighbor search?
questions.answer: A FAISS flat index for exact nearest-neighbor search.
evidence: FAISS flat index for exact nearest-neighbor search

questions.question: What token-level F1 did answers from hybrid-retrieved context achieve?
questions.answer: 0.74, compared with 0.68 for semantic-only retrieval.

questions.question: Which retrieval method had the lowest Mean Reciprocal Rank, and how far below hybrid retrieval was it?
questions.answer: BM25-only retrieval, with an MRR of 0.71 versus 0.89 for hybrid retrieval, a gap of 0.18.

questions.question: How were the 0.6 and 0.4 weights chosen?
questions.answer: By manual tuning on a held-out validation subset rather than a formal hyperparameter search.
evidence: was chosen based on manual tuning on a held-out validation subset

questions.question: What future work do the authors suggest?
questions.answer: Learned combination weights, reranking models, and evaluation on a broader range of document domains including legal and medical text.
evidence: Future work should explore learned combination weights
